about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Peposo (Tuscan Slow-Cooked Black Pepper Beef)
recipes.summary: A Tuscan beef braise driven by a lot of black pepper, red wine and tomato, cooked until spoon tender.

items: 800g beef chuck, cut into large chunks

steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, in batches.
Return all the beef, add the garlic, pepper, tomato paste, wine, stock, rosemary and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer, until bubbling gently.
Cover and braise for 2 hours, until the beef is very tender. Add the potato for the last 40 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve with the pan juices.
notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Polpettone (Italian Baked Meatloaf with Peas and Tomato)
recipes.summary: A baked Italian meatloaf of beef and pork with parsley and cheese, finished in tomato sauce with peas.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Mix the minces, egg, breadcrumbs, cheese, parsley, garlic, oregano and 1 tsp salt and shape into a loaf in a baking dish.
Pour the tomatoes around the loaf. Bake for 45 minutes.
Scatter in the peas, bake 10 minutes more, until the loaf reaches 75°C in the centre.
Rest 10 minutes, slice and spoon over the sauce.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Maiale al Latte (Pork Slow-Cooked in Milk and Sage)
recipes.summary: A Bolognese braise where pork shoulder cooks gently in milk until the sauce turns nutty and thick.
steps: Brown the pork all over in the oil and butter in a heavy pot for 10 minutes. Add the garlic, sage, lemon zest, 1 tsp salt and the milk.

Simmer, partly covered, on low for 1 hour 45 minutes, turning the pork now and then, until the milk has reduced to a thick golden sauce and the pork is very tender. Add the potato for the last 30 minutes.
Slice the pork and serve with the sauce spooned over.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk. The sauce looks curdled; it is meant to.

recipes.title: Spezzatino di Manzo con Piselli (Italian Beef and Pea Stew)
recipes.summary: A gentle Italian beef stew with tomato, carrot and sweet peas, good with soft polenta.
steps: Brown the beef in the oil for 8 minutes. Lift out, then cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the wine and stock. Return the beef, cover and simmer for 1 hour 45 minutes, until tender. Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes.
Cook the polenta in 4 cups of salted water for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick. Serve the stew over the polenta.
notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Poule au Pot (French Poached Chicken with Winter Vegetables)
recipes.summary: Henri IV's Sunday chicken, gently poached with leek, carrot and swede in its own broth.
steps: Put the chicken, onion, bay leaves, peppercorns and 2 tsp salt in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 40 minutes, skimming.
Add the carrot, swede and leek and simmer for 30 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C at the thigh and the vegetables are tender.
Carve the chicken, serve with vegetables and a ladle of broth, with the mustard and parsley.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free. Keep the broth for soup.

recipes.title: Tian Provencal (Baked Provencal Vegetable Gratin)
recipes.summary: Slices of zucchini, eggplant, tomato and potato layered upright and baked with thyme and olive oil.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Soften the onion and garlic in 1 tbsp oil for 6 minutes and spread over a baking dish with the lentils.
Stand the sliced vegetables in rows over the top, drizzle with the remaining oil, thyme, 1 tsp salt and pepper.
Cover and bake for 35 minutes. Uncover, add the cheese and bake 15 minutes more, until golden and the potato is tender.
notes: Vegetarian. Contains milk.

recipes.title: Soupe au Pistou (Provencal Vegetable and White Bean Soup)
recipes.summary: A summer vegetable and bean soup finished with a basil, garlic and cheese pistou stirred through.
steps: Soften the onion in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes, then add the carrot, zucchini, potato, beans and stock. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook for 8 minutes, until tender.
Crush or blitz the basil, garlic, cheese and remaining oil with a pinch of salt into a paste. Stir through the soup off the heat.
notes: Vegetarian. Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Gigot d'Agneau aux Anchois (French Roast Leg of Lamb with Anchovy and Garlic)
recipes.summary: A leg of lamb studded with garlic, rosemary and anchovy, roasted until pink and rested well.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut small slits in the lamb and push in the garlic, anchovy and rosemary. Rub with the oil and 1 tsp salt.
Roast on a bed of potato for 20 minutes, then reduce to 170°C (150°C fan) and roast for 1 hour 10 minutes, until a thermometer reads 60°C for medium.
Rest the lamb for 20 minutes. Simmer the wine and stock in the tin for 8 minutes to a sauce. Carve and serve.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Contains fish (anchovy).
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Cuisses de Canard aux Lentilles (Roast Duck Legs with Lentils)
recipes.summary: Crisp roasted duck legs on a bed of lentils cooked with carrot, thyme and white wine.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Salt the duck legs, set on a rack and roast for 70 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the meat tender.
Meanwhile, cook the onion, carrot and garlic in 1 tbsp duck fat from the tray for 6 minutes. Add the lentils, wine, stock and thyme and simmer for 30 minutes, until tender. Stir in the mustard.
Serve the duck on the lentils.
notes: Food safety: duck must reach 75°C in the thickest part with clear juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Baeckeoffe (Alsatian Baker's Oven Casserole)
recipes.summary: Three meats layered with potato, leek and onion and baked slowly in white wine, the classic Alsatian Sunday pot.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Season all the meat with 2 tsp salt, pepper and the garlic.
Layer half the potato, then the vegetables, then the meat, then the rest of the vegetables and potato in a lidded casserole, adding the bay and thyme.
Pour in the wine and 1 cup water. Cover and bake for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the meat is tender.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Beef and lamb must be tender and above 70°C.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Steak Frites (Bistro Pan-Seared Steak with Oven Chips and Pepper Butter)
recipes.summary: The bistro classic: a well-rested seared steak with crisp oven chips and a quick pepper butter.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chips with the oil and 1 tsp salt and bake for 35 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Mash the butter with the pepper, parsley and garlic.
Pat the steaks dry and sear in a very hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes a side for medium. Rest 5 minutes.
Top the steaks with the butter and serve with the chips and rocket.
notes: Food safety: sear steak on the outside; whole steaks are safe at 63°C with a rest, and any pieces must be cooked through if cut or minced. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

recipes.title: Gratin de Courgettes (French Zucchini and Egg Gratin)
recipes.summary: A custardy zucchini gratin baked with onion, thyme and cheese, a light bistro main with a salad.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the zucchini and cook for 8 minutes, until just soft.
Whisk the eggs, cream, half the cheese, thyme and 1/2 tsp salt. Fold in the zucchini and pour into a baking dish.
Top with the breadcrumbs and remaining cheese. Bake for 25 minutes, until set and golden.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian. Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Lancashire Hotpot (Lamb and Potato Pot)
recipes.summary: Lamb and onion in a rich stock beneath overlapping golden potato slices, a northern English classic.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Toss the lamb with the flour and layer in a casserole with the onion and carrot.
Pour over the stock and worcestershire sauce, add the thyme and 1 tsp salt. Lay the potato in overlapping rows on top and brush with the butter.
Cover and bake for 2 hours. Uncover and bake 25 minutes, until the potato is golden and the lamb tender.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Cornish Pasty (Beef, Potato and Swede in Short Pastry)
recipes.summary: A hand-sized pasty of beef, potato, swede and onion baked in a sturdy pastry crust.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour with 1 tsp salt, add about 1/3 cup cold water to make a firm dough and rest it while you prep the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the beef, potato, swede, onion, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Roll the dough and cut four 20cm rounds.
Pile filling onto each, fold over and crimp the edge. Brush with the egg.
Bake for 15 minutes, then at 170°C (150°C fan) for 40 minutes, until golden and the beef is cooked through.
notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Pasties must be steaming hot throughout.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Cawl (Welsh Lamb and Root Vegetable Broth)
recipes.summary: A Welsh lamb and root vegetable broth, thick with leek and potato, traditionally eaten from a bowl with bread.
steps: Put the lamb, onion, stock, thyme and 1 tsp salt in a pot, bring to a simmer and cook gently for 1 hour, skimming.
Add the carrot, swede and potato and simmer for 25 minutes. Add the leek and cook 10 minutes more, until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the parsley and serve with bread.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Beef and Ale Casserole with Herb Dumplings
recipes.summary: A deep brown beef and dark beer casserole with fluffy herb dumplings steamed on top.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown the beef in the oil in batches. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 6 minutes, stir in the plain flour and tomato paste, then the beer and stock.
Cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours, until tender.
Rub the butter into the self-raising flour with the thyme and 1/2 tsp salt, add 1/3 cup cold water and form 6 dumplings.
Set on top of the casserole, cover and cook for 20 minutes, until puffed.
notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk. Beer is cooked off but not fully removed.

recipes.title: Leek and Potato Gratin with Wholegrain Mustard
recipes.summary: A creamy baked leek and potato gratin with mustard and a golden cheese crust, good as a vegetarian main with greens.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Warm the cream, milk, mustard, garlic and 1 tsp salt together.
Layer the potato, leek and spinach in a baking dish, pouring over the creamy mix as you go. Top with the cheese.
Cover and bake for 40 minutes, uncover and bake 20 minutes more, until the potato is tender and golden.
notes: Vegetarian. Contains milk.

recipes.title: Lentejas con Chorizo (Spanish Lentil and Chorizo Stew)
recipes.summary: A homely Spanish lentil pot with chorizo, potato, carrot and smoked paprika.
steps: Cook the chorizo in a pot for 4 minutes, until it releases its oil. Add the onion, carrot, capsicum and garlic and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the paprika, lentils, bay leaf, potato and stock. Simmer for 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender and the stew thickened.
Season with salt and serve with bread.
notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Caldereta de Cordero (Spanish Lamb Stew with Peppers and Wine)
recipes.summary: A Spanish shepherd's lamb stew with capsicum, garlic, paprika and white wine.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil in batches, 8 minutes. Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic in the same pot for 6 minutes. Stir in the paprika.
Add the wine, tomatoes, bay and 1 tsp salt and return the lamb. Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the potato and simmer 30 minutes more, until the lamb and potato are tender.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Kavurma (Turkish Slow-Fried Lamb with Tomato and Peppers)
recipes.summary: Lamb cooked down in its own juices with onion, tomato and peppers until tender and glossy, eaten with rice or bread.
steps: Heat the oil and brown the lamb in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 10 minutes. Add the onion, capsicum, garlic, cumin and chilli and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and 1 tsp salt, cover and cook on low for 1 hour 10 minutes, until the lamb is very tender and the juices thick.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, drain and serve with the lamb.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Moroccan Lamb Kefta Tagine with Baked Eggs
recipes.summary: Spiced lamb meatballs simmered in a cumin and paprika tomato sauce, with eggs set on top and bread to mop up.
steps: Mix the lamb, onion, half the garlic, half the cumin, the paprika, coriander and 1 tsp salt and roll into 20 small balls.

Brown the balls in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the remaining garlic and cumin, the cinnamon, tomatoes and 1/2 cup water and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the meatballs cooked through.
Make 4 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 6 minutes, until the whites are set. Serve with bread.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Contains egg. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Kapusta z Kielbasa (Polish Braised Cabbage with Smoked Sausage and Potato)
recipes.summary: A Polish one-pot of soft braised cabbage, smoked sausage and potato, seasoned with caraway and a splash of vinegar.
steps: Brown the sausage in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the cabbage, potato, caraway, paprika, stock and 1/2 tsp salt. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the cabbage and potato are tender.
Stir in the vinegar and serve.
notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Pierogi Ruskie (Polish Potato and Cheese Dumplings with Fried Onion)
recipes.summary: Tender dumplings filled with potato and ricotta, boiled and finished in butter with caramelised onion.
steps: Mix the flour, egg, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup warm water into a soft dough. Cover and set aside.
Cook half the onion in 20g butter for 8 minutes. Mix into the mash with the ricotta and 1/2 tsp salt.
Roll the dough thin, cut 8cm rounds, fill with the potato mix and pinch to seal.
Boil in batches for 4 minutes, until they float. Fry the remaining onion in the remaining butter until golden and toss the dumplings through. Serve with sour cream.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian. Contains egg, gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Karelian Stew (Finnish Slow-Baked Beef and Pork with Allspice)
recipes.summary: A Finnish stew of beef and pork baked low for hours with onion and allspice, served with mash.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Toss the meat with the flour and 2 tsp salt and layer in a casserole with the onion, allspice and bay.
Pour over the stock. Cover tightly and bake for 3 hours, until the meat is tender and the juices rich.
Mash the potato with the butter and a splash of the cooking juices, then serve the stew over the mash.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Beef must be tender and above 70°C.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Stegt Flaesk med Persillesovs (Danish Crisp Pork Belly with Parsley Sauce)
recipes.summary: The Danish national dish: crisp fried pork belly slices with potatoes and a creamy parsley sauce.
steps: Fry the pork belly slices in a dry pan over medium heat for 8 minutes a side, until golden and crisp. Drain on paper.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute and whisk in the milk. Simmer for 5 minutes, add the parsley, 1/2 tsp salt and pepper.
Serve the pork with the potatoes and sauce.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Chicken and Dumplings (American Southern Comfort Stew)
recipes.summary: A creamy chicken and vegetable stew topped with tender drop dumplings, an American family favourite.
steps: Brown the chicken in the butter for 6 minutes. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 6 minutes. Stir in the plain flour, then the stock and cream. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Rub the cold butter into the self-raising flour with 1/2 tsp salt, stir in the milk and spoon in 8 dumplings.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are cooked through and the chicken reaches 75°C.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Sancocho (Colombian-Style Beef, Yuca and Plantain Stew)
recipes.summary: A big pot of beef broth with corn, plantain and potato, eaten as a hearty Latin American family dinner.
steps: Put the beef, onion, garlic, cumin, stock, 1 tsp salt and 2 cups water in a pot. Simmer for 1 hour, until nearly tender.
Add the potato, carrot, plantain and corn and simmer for 30 minutes more.
Serve with coriander and lime.
notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Lamb Cutlets with Salsa Verde and Crisp Roast Potatoes
recipes.summary: Grilled lamb cutlets with a sharp parsley, caper and anchovy salsa verde and golden roast potatoes.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato with 1 tbsp oil and 1 tsp salt and roast for 40 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Chop the parsley, capers, anchovy and garlic finely, then mix with the mustard, lemon juice and 2 tbsp oil.
Season the cutlets and grill or pan fry for 3 minutes a side for medium, until browned. Rest for 5 minutes and serve with the salsa and potatoes.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Contains fish (anchovy).
Dairy-free and gluten-free.
